questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The life and teachings of the Dalai Lama in India
How to relax by watching films before bed
Research showing meditation can change the brain
Why Tibetan monks choose to live in monasteries
questions.why: They discuss experiments proving for the first time that meditation can actually change the brain.

questions.q: What is Sam's first idea of meditation?
options: A kind of exercise class at the local gym
A religious ceremony that takes place in a temple
A way of sleeping during the day to rest the mind
Sitting cross-legged on the floor thinking of nothing
questions.why: Sam asks if it's just people sitting cross-legged on the floor, thinking of nothing.

questions.q: What did the Dalai Lama challenge Richard Davidson to do?
options: Use neuroscience to study kindness and compassion
Stop studying depression and anxiety in patients
Become a Buddhist monk and live in a monastery
Write a best-selling book about meditation
questions.why: He asked why Davidson couldn't use the same tools to study kindness and compassion.

questions.q: What did the monks do during the test?
options: They tried to think of nothing
They solved difficult puzzles
They sent loving thoughts to everyone equally
They focused only on their breathing
questions.why: Sam says they sent loving thoughts to friends, enemies, strangers and themselves.

questions.q: What was surprising about the monks' gamma waves?
options: They were much lower than in normal people
They lasted minutes instead of under a second
They only appeared while the monks were sleeping
They disappeared completely after meditation
questions.why: Neil says for us a flash of insight might last under a second, but for the monks the waves lasted minutes.

questions.q: According to Richard Davidson, which brain circuits can meditation change?
options: Those that control attention and emotion
Those that control movement
Those that control memory only
Those that control sleep
questions.why: He says the circuits include those important for regulating attention and regulating emotion.

questions.q: Why is Sam doubtful at first that meditation could help him?
options: He thinks it is boring and a waste of his time
He doesn't really believe in science or scientists
He thinks he is too old to learn something new
He works and can't spend thousands of hours on it
questions.why: He says the monks spend thousands of hours meditating, but he has to go to work.

questions.q: What did the experiment show about new meditators?
options: They saw no change at all, even after two weeks
They needed at least three hours a day to see results
30 minutes a day increased their loving kindness
They became more upset and anxious at first
questions.why: Neil says 30 minutes of meditation a day significantly increased loving kindness in new meditators.
